**Rates/COE inputs.** Fed funds 3.75–4.00% (hike 09-15/16, the macro regime memo 2026-10-03); UST10 5.24% (FRED DGS10 2026-10-01); COE 10.2% = 5.24 + USD ERP 4.5–5.5% mid (VAL_BANKS).

**Reported base (primary sources).** FY25 (Q4-25 8-K 2026-01-14 ex-99.1): NI $30,509M, EPS $3.81, ROE 10.6%, ROTCE 14.2%, eff 62%, NIY 2.01%, NII $60,096M (+7.2%), provision $5,675M vs NCO $5,631M (0.50% of avg loans), CET1 11.4%, BVPS $38.44, TBVPS $28.73; Q4-25 cx-capital return $8.4B. H1-26 (10-Q 2026-06-30): revenue $61,830M (+11.0%), NII $31,742M (+9.0%), noninterest income $30,088M (+13.2%), expense $37,158M (+6.3%), provision $2,703M, NI $17,658M, EPS $2.31, eff 60.1%. Q2-26 (8-K 2026-07-14 ex-99.1/99.2): NI $9,074M, EPS $1.21, ROE 12.71%, ROTCE 17.03%, eff 58.72% FTE, NIY 2.08% (ex-Markets 2.57%), loans $1,217.6B (+6.1% y/y), deposits $2,025.1B, card NCO 3.55% (vs 3.82% yr ago; delinquencies better 5th straight qtr y/y), ACL $14.3B, CET1 11.2% std, consumer rate-paid-on-deposits 0.48% (vs 0.58% yr ago), ~51% of consumer deposits non/low-interest checking.

**Build FY26E→FY28E.** NII $65.5B→$67B→flat (2027 cuts cushioned by deposit-beta lag; ex-Markets yield 2.57% still ~+13bp y/y = securities/swap repricing tailwind). Fees +6%/yr after H1 +13%. Revenue $127B→$133B→$139B; expense $76.5B→$78.5B→$79.5B (eff 60.1%→58.5%→57%; H1 comp +5.2% vs revenue +11% = operating leverage). Provision ≈ through-cycle NCO ~0.55% of loans ≈ $6.5B FY28E; ACL 1.17%→~1.05%. Tax 19.6%. NI ~$36B/$38B/$41B; EPS $4.90/$5.40/$5.85 (diluted shares −4%/yr buyback). **Sustainable ROE ~13.2%, ROTCE ~18%.** Total return ≈100% of income → common equity ~flat (~$276B); TBVPS growth is share-shrink (−5.6% y/y shares). g 1.5% ≈ ROE×(1−payout) (VAL_BANKS rule 5); CET1 11.2% is ~40bp above buffers — buyback leg is the constraint. Load-bearing cited: NIM/funding (10-Q R2, ex-99.2), efficiency (8-K), card credit (8-K).

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.markdown: The market narrative: BAC is the slow-growth deposit monster whose bond/swap drag caps ROE near 12% and efficiency at ~60%, so 1.4x book is fair and no re-rating is deserved.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** NII growth is a rate-cycle artifact that reverses when 2027 cuts land; efficiency is stuck near 60% (wages, tech); card NCOs will re-lever-up; and 1.37x P/BV prices all of it — no re-rating left.

**Why wrong:** (a) NII +9% y/y H1-26 was delivered THROUGH the 2024–26 cuts (10-Q) because deposit funding costs keep falling (consumer rate-paid 0.48% vs 0.58%, ex-99.2) while the securities/swap book reprices up (ex-Markets yield 2.57%, +13bp y/y) — a multi-year tailwind; the 51% non/low-interest checking mix cushions 2027 cuts to low-single-digit NII growth, not a rollover. (b) Efficiency 62%→58.7% in four quarters on revenue +15% is a structural cost curve (digital, branch-to-digital), not headcount optics — H1 comp +5.2% y/y vs revenue +11% is operating leverage; 57% by FY28 is below the 360bp/yr pace. (c) Credit improves, not turns: card NCO 3.55% vs 3.82% y/y, delinquencies 5 qtrs better, consumer NCO 0.86% — the normalization the market fears is behind us. ROTCE 14.2%→17.0% (FY25→Q2-26) is a re-rating being REPORTED in the numbers.

**What proves us wrong:** ROTCE 4.2% with reserve build; UST10 ≥5.7% → COE ≥10.7% and warranted P/TBV below traded 1.83x.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: observable now; each cites a source
sections.markdown:
1. UST10 5.24% and pressing up (FRED DGS10 2026-10-01): +~50bp → COE ~10.7% → warranted P/TBV at 18% ROTCE ~1.70x < 1.83x traded — discount-rate path kills the re-rating regardless of BAC execution (the live trip that hit JPM-001).
2. H1-26 revenue +11% rides a markets/IB boom (IB +50%, S&T $7.1B, 8-K); ~$3–4B/yr fee normalisation with comp +5% snaps efficiency above 60% — falsifies the structural claim.
3. ~100% payout is funded by CET1 drawdown 11.5→11.2% (8-K); any credit/regulatory reset forces a buyback cut and the share-shrink engine (shares −5.6% y/y) stalls.
4. Loans +6.1% y/y on 1.17% ACL at cycle-low card NCOs — model underwrites normalization at today's level; a 2027 consumer re-leveraging to 4.5% NCO reverses the reserve tailwind.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: 2029, down ~25%: the 2027 cuts landed deeper than the deposit-beta cushion — NII rolled over as the securities-repricing tailwind exhausted before deposit costs bottomed; efficiency stalled at 58% on wage inflation; a card cycle to 4.5% NCO forced reserve builds at CET1 11.2%, so buybacks were cut, book stopped compounding, and the 1.83x TBV premium de-rated toward 1.3x. The re-rating I called structural was half cyclical revenue windfall — the same weak joint Drew found in JPM-001, and 2027 came earlier than my horizon admitted.
